newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks drop 2.12 pct on foreign selling.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks drop 2.12 pct on foreign selling.

text.p: Battered Thai stocks, already at their lowest levels in over three years, fell 2.12 percent in thin trade shortly after the market reopened on Monday afternoon as foreigners continued to unload shares, brokers said.
"Foreign investors are still selling. There's no fresh incentive to boost investment," a broker said.
The volatile index slipped 2.12 percent to 913.12 points only two minutes after trading resumed in the afternoon.
By 0757 GMT the index dropped further to 912.47, down 20.39 points.
"The market isn't active as it lacks fresh and positive news to boost the market," said a broker at Ekachart Finance and Securities.
Expectations of poor corporate third quarter earnings, especially in the banking sector, were causing foreign investors to sell, brokers said.
